subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace containment a default enforced security boundary, or keep host-wide filesystem access as trusted personal-agent behavior with opt-in sandbox/workspaceOnly controls?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves legacy host-wide file access unless operators opt into workspaceOnly or sandboxing, so automation cannot safely choose the new default, compatibility story, or exec/sandbox scope.

options.title: Define a default hard boundary
options.body: Recommended: keep this issue open while maintainers choose the default containment, migration, docs, and exec/sandbox policy needed to make per-agent workspace isolation real.

options.title: Keep trusted-host defaults
options.body: Maintain the current personal-assistant trust model and close only after explicitly deciding that docs plus opt-in sandbox/workspaceOnly are sufficient.

options.title: Scope to a narrower subset
options.body: Land a limited file-tool hardening PR while leaving this issue open or linking a broader canonical item for exec and local-user isolation.

recommendation.title: Define a default hard boundary
recommendation.body: Recommended: keep this issue open while maintainers choose the default containment, migration, docs, and exec/sandbox policy needed to make per-agent workspace isolation real.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the optional filesystem workspace guard and is the strongest current history signal for the security/default policy boundary.
